shipped_rows.title_o: Silence is Golden: Effect of Encouragement in Motivating the Weak Link in an Online Exercise Video Game

blind_target.evidence_quote: Recent research on exercise with virtually present partners found that encouragement attenuated the Köhler effect, which boosts task motivation for weaker group members in conjunctive tasks. The current study replicated and extended previous research, comparing exclusive (e.g. “you can do it”) and inclusive encouragement (e.g. “we can do it”) as potential moderators of the Köhler effect.
blind_target.outcome_quote: A significant motivation gain was observed in all partnered conditions compared to the control, and exclusive encouragement from a virtually present partner attenuated motivation gains. However, inclusive encouragement did not, and encouragement from an audible trainer boosted exercise motivation over the control group.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Abstract states the previous finding that encouragement attenuated motivation gains and reports the corresponding attenuation under exclusive encouragement. Inclusive encouragement and audible trainer are extensions; no explicit contrast with the original is stated.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract says the study tested a prior encouragement finding, but it does not cite or otherwise identify the original work. The supplied shipped original is a plausible match, yet the abstract alone cannot establish whether it is the same original; the full reference/context linking this finding to Irwin, Feltz, and Kerr is needed.
